definitions.explanation: An integer that is not divisible by two, such as 1, 3, 5, 7, etc.

examples.japanese: {奇数|きすう}⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{偶数|ぐうすう}→偶数：00077_guusuu⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{判定|はんてい}→判定：09767_hantei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I determine whether it's an odd or even number.
3 is an odd number, and 4 is an even number.
Trash can only be put out on odd-numbered days.

notes:
{奇数|きすう} means odd number — any integer not divisible by two (1, 3, 5, 7, etc.). The kanji {奇|き} means "strange/unusual" and ⟦{数|すう}→数：03360_suu⟧ means "number."

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{偶数|ぐうすう}→偶数：00077_guusuu⟧: even number

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {奇数|きすう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: odd-numbered days
- {奇数|きすう}⟦{月|がつ}→月：30418_gatsu⟧: odd-numbered months (January, March, etc.)
- {奇数|きすう}⟦{番号|ばんごう}→番号：02939_bangou⟧: odd-numbered

RELATED MATH TERMS:
- ⟦{自然数|しぜんすう}→自然数：23397_shizensuu⟧: natural number
- ⟦{整数|せいすう}→整数：04328_seisuu⟧: integer
- ⟦{素数|そすう}→素数：20727_sosuu⟧: prime number
- ⟦{分数|ぶんすう}→分数：06952_bunsuu⟧: fraction

CULTURAL NOTE:
Odd numbers are traditionally considered lucky in Japan ({吉数|きっすう}). Gift money (⟦{祝儀|しゅうぎ}→祝儀：06225_shuugi⟧) is typically given in odd-numbered amounts (10,000, 30,000, 50,000 yen).
